laws.fullDescription: The Oceans Act (SC 1996 c 31) gives the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans authority to designate Marine Protected Areas. Canada targets 25% ocean protection by 2025. Fishing, anchoring, and discharging pollutants are prohibited in many MPAs. Transport Canada guidelines require minimum 400m distance from Southern Resident killer whales (critically endangered) in BC waters; whale watching tours in the Gulf Islands regularly receive compliance orders. The Johnstone Strait is a critical killer whale habitat.
laws.penalty: Up to $500,000 fines for commercial violations of MPA regulations
laws.exceptions: Indigenous fishing rights exercised under treaty; permitted scientific research

quiz.q: Marine Protected Area regulations in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under environmental law.

laws.title: Protecting Canadians from Online Crime Act (Bill C-13)
laws.subtitle: Cyberbullying tools, non-consensual images, and new investigative powers enacted 2014
laws.fullDescription: The Protecting Canadians from Online Crime Act (SC 2014 c 31) criminalized non-consensual sharing of intimate images, created electronic production orders and transmission data warrants, and made it an offence to make or distribute malware. Passed in response to the Rehtaeh Parsons (Nova Scotia) and Amanda Todd (BC) cyberbullying tragedies. Social media platforms must respond to Canadian court production orders. The Act also created a new offence for using computers to commit sexual exploitation.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years for non-consensual image sharing; up to 10 years for cybercrime tools
laws.exceptions: Lawful disclosure by law enforcement with proper court authorization

quiz.q: Online crime and cyberbullying laws in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Migratory Birds Regulations — Federal Hunting Permit
laws.subtitle: Federal Migratory Game Bird Hunting Permit required in addition to provincial licence
laws.fullDescription: Hunting migratory birds in Canada requires a federal Migratory Game Bird Hunting Permit (Environment and Climate Change Canada) in addition to any provincial hunting licence. Non-toxic shot (steel, bismuth, tungsten) must be used for all migratory bird hunting — lead shot banned to protect waterfowl and bald eagles (which scavenge shot game). Bag limits are set annually based on Canadian Wildlife Service population surveys. Canada Geese are strictly managed.
laws.penalty: Up to $100,000 fine for Migratory Birds Convention Act violations; forfeiture of equipment
laws.exceptions: Indigenous peoples with treaty rights; licensed researchers with scientific permits

quiz.q: Federal migratory bird hunting regulations fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: E-Scooter and Micro-mobility — Provincial Pilot Programs
laws.subtitle: E-scooter rules vary widely; helmets required; many cities have rental permit programs
laws.fullDescription: E-scooter regulations vary significantly by province. Ontario permits e-scooters in pilot municipalities (max 24km/h, helmet required). BC allows them on most roads (max 32km/h). Alberta has municipality-by-municipality rules. Quebec bans them on public roads except in designated zones. Rental scooter programs (Lime, Bird) operate under municipal permits. Riding without a helmet in required zones results in fines. E-scooters are not permitted on most highways or expressways.
laws.penalty: $100-$250 fines for helmet violations; $200+ for operating in prohibited areas
laws.exceptions: Private property operation; provincial or municipal approved pilot areas

quiz.q: E-scooter regulations in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under traffic law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Mailing Prohibited Items
laws.subtitle: Mailing drugs, firearms, or dangerous items is criminal; cannabis cannot be mailed internationally
laws.fullDescription: The Criminal Code and Canada Post Corporation Act restrict mailing prohibited items. Canada Post reports packages suspected to contain drugs, explosives, or firearms to CBSA and police. The CBSA inspects international mail at Gateway facilities in Montreal and Toronto. Mailing cannabis across international borders remains criminal even post-legalization. Mailing lithium batteries exceeding size limits is restricted for aviation safety. Sending counterfeit goods through the mail is both criminal and civil copyright infringement.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years for mailing prohibited items related to drugs or firearms
laws.exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical distributors; authorized law enforcement shipments with documentation

quiz.q: Mailing prohibited items in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Extortion (s.346)
laws.subtitle: Threatening harm unless demands are met carries up to life imprisonment
laws.fullDescription: Section 346 of the Criminal Code makes extortion — intentionally inducing any person to do anything by threats, accusations, or menace — punishable by up to life imprisonment if the extortion is accompanied by a firearm. Non-firearm extortion carries up to 14 years. Romance scams (catfishing then threatening to release images), ransomware attacks, and sextortion targeting Canadians have sharply increased. RCMP and provincial cybercrime units handle these cases.
laws.penalty: Up to life imprisonment if firearm involved; up to 14 years for non-firearm extortion
laws.exceptions: Lawful demands for payment of legitimate debts do not constitute extortion

quiz.q: Extortion in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Safe Food for Canadians Act — Food Safety Regulations
laws.subtitle: Unsafe food or fraudulent food safety claims are criminal; CFIA enforces recalls
laws.fullDescription: The Safe Food for Canadians Act (SC 2012 c 24) and accompanying Regulations (SOR/2018-108) require food businesses to have documented preventive control plans (similar to HACCP). The CFIA conducts inspections and orders mandatory recalls for Listeria, E. coli, Salmonella contamination. Selling adulterated, falsely labelled, or unsafe food is criminal under the Food and Drugs Act. The 2008 Maple Leaf Listeria outbreak (23 deaths) drove major regulatory reform.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; fines up to $5 million for corporations
laws.exceptions: Personal and domestic food production not entering the commercial supply chain
laws.sourceLabel: Safe Food for Canadians Act SC 2012

quiz.q: Food safety law in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Criminal Records and Record Suspension
laws.subtitle: Pardons replaced by record suspension; US border access not guaranteed even after suspension
laws.fullDescription: The Criminal Records Act (RSC 1985 c C-47) allows applying for record suspension (formerly pardon) after completing sentence and waiting 3-10 years. A suspension removes the record from the RCMP main database. However, US Customs uses historical CPIC data including suspended records — a Canadian with any criminal conviction may be denied US entry. Applying for a US waiver (I-192 or I-194) is a separate process through CBP. Some convictions (sexual offences against minors, multiple offences) are ineligible.
laws.penalty: A criminal record without suspension affects employment, professional licences, and US entry
laws.exceptions: Certain serious offences are ineligible for suspension regardless of time elapsed

quiz.q: Criminal record suspension in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act (CFPOA)
laws.subtitle: Canadian companies and individuals cannot bribe foreign officials
laws.fullDescription: The Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act (SC 1998 c 34) makes it a criminal offence for Canadians or Canadian companies to offer or give a benefit to a foreign public official to influence a business advantage. Canada has actively prosecuted corporations under this legislation, including SNC-Lavalin's controversial 2019 deferred prosecution agreement over bribery in Libya. Facilitation payments were removed as an exception in 2013. Canada participates in OECD Anti-Bribery Convention monitoring.
laws.penalty: Up to 14 years imprisonment; unlimited corporate fines; debarment from government contracts
laws.exceptions: Facilitation payments no longer exempted since 2013

quiz.q: Canada's foreign corruption law falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: National Parks — Wildfire and Campfire Safety
laws.subtitle: Campfire bans enforced in national and provincial parks; open flame restrictions during high danger
laws.fullDescription: Parks Canada and provincial parks impose campfire restrictions and bans during high fire danger periods. In national parks, open fires outside designated fire pits are prohibited year-round. During fire bans, propane stoves may be restricted in some areas. BC Wildfire Service issues province-wide prohibition orders. The 2023 Jasper wildfire (which destroyed 30% of the town) and the 2016 Fort McMurray fire (88,000 evacuated) demonstrate the catastrophic risk of fire in Canada's boreal forests.
laws.penalty: $50,000-$1,000,000 fines; potential criminal negligence charges if fire causes damage
laws.exceptions: Designated campfire rings during non-ban periods; gas/propane stoves allowed in most ban situations

quiz.q: Wildfire and campfire safety regulations in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under environmental law.

laws.title: Refugee Protection — IRPA and False Claims
laws.subtitle: Canada accepts refugee claimants at border and inland; false claims are criminal
laws.fullDescription: The Immigration and Refugee Protection Act s.96-101 establishes Canada's refugee system administered by the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB). Persons fearing persecution on Convention grounds may claim refugee protection at a port of entry or inland. The US-Canada Safe Third Country Agreement (STCA) — upheld by the Supreme Court in 2023 — requires claimants arriving from the US to make claims there (unless crossing an irregular land border). Making a false refugee claim is criminal.
laws.penalty: Up to 14 years for human smuggling; false claim results in removal and 5-year application bar
laws.exceptions: STCA exceptions for family members; LGBTQ+ claimants fleeing US state-level restrictions argued

quiz.q: Refugee protection law in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Hoax Regarding Terrorist Activity (s.83.231)
laws.subtitle: Making a fake bomb threat or hoax about terrorist activity is a criminal offence
laws.fullDescription: Section 83.231 of the Criminal Code makes it an offence to convey information that one knows is false to cause fear of terrorist activity. This includes false bomb threats, fake anthrax letters, and social media hoaxes threatening mass casualties. Post-pandemic, threats against hospitals and schools via social media have resulted in prosecutions under this section and under s.264.1 (uttering threats). School administrators are required to report threats.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment
laws.exceptions: Clearly fictional works identified as such; threat assessment training exercises with authorization

quiz.q: Hoax terrorist threats in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Stunt Driving — Immediately Licence Suspended on Roadside
laws.subtitle: Stunt driving (50+km/h over limit, racing, doing donuts) triggers roadside licence seizure
laws.fullDescription: Ontario and other provinces have stunt driving laws (Ontario's HTA s.172) that deem certain actions as stunt driving: exceeding the speed limit by 40-50+km/h, street racing, performing donuts, or cutting off other vehicles for amusement. Police immediately seize the driver's licence for 30 days and impound the vehicle for 14 days on first offence. A stunt driving conviction carries a minimum 1-year licence suspension and a fine of $2,000-$10,000.
laws.penalty: Immediate roadside suspension; vehicle impoundment; $2,000-$10,000 fine on conviction; 1-year+ licence suspension
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles on active emergency calls

quiz.q: Stunt driving laws in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under traffic law.

laws.title: Off-Road Vehicle Regulations — ATVs and Snowmobiles
laws.subtitle: Registration and helmet required; trespassing on private land with ORV is criminal
laws.fullDescription: Off-road vehicles (ATVs, snowmobiles, dirt bikes) are regulated provincially. Ontario requires ORV permits; Quebec licenses snowmobiles separately ($80/year registration). Helmets mandatory for operators and passengers in most provinces. Operating ORVs on public roads generally prohibited except at designated crossings. Snowmobiles on private land without landowner permission constitute trespass and criminal mischief. Ontario's Trespass to Property Act gives landowners authority to remove trespassers.
laws.penalty: $200-$1,000 fines for unregistered ORV; $500+ for operating on prohibited public roads
laws.exceptions: Designated ORV trails; authorized crossings of public roads; farmer operating on own land

quiz.q: Off-road vehicle regulations in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under environmental law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Uttering Threats (s.264.1)
laws.subtitle: Threatening death or serious bodily harm to any person is a criminal offence
laws.fullDescription: Section 264.1 of the Criminal Code makes it an offence to utter, convey, or cause a person to receive a threat to cause death or serious bodily harm, to burn or destroy property, or to kill or harm an animal. Threats made online, via text, or in person are all captured. The Crown does not need to prove the accused intended to carry out the threat — only that they intended the words to be taken as a threat. School, workplace, and social media threats have significantly increased prosecutions.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment on indictment; up to 18 months on summary conviction
laws.exceptions: Clearly hyperbolic expressions of frustration without intent to intimidate; artistic expression

quiz.q: Uttering threats in Canada falls under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Organic Products Regulations — Organic Labelling
laws.subtitle: Products labelled organic must be certified by accredited body; 95% threshold applies
laws.fullDescription: Canada's Organic Products Regulations (SOR/2009-176) require that products labelled as organic meet Canadian Organic Standards and be certified by a CFIA-accredited certification body. The 95% organic content threshold applies to the organic label; 70-95% may use contains organic ingredients. Non-compliant organic claims constitute misleading advertising under the Competition Act. Imported organic products must meet CFIA equivalency arrangement requirements.
laws.penalty: Fines for misleading organic labelling; removal from shelves; Competition Act sanctions
laws.exceptions: Products not crossing provincial or international borders may be exempt from federal regulations

quiz.q: Organic labelling rules in Canada fall under which legal category?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under environmental law.

laws.title: Criminal Code — Voyeurism (s.162)
laws.subtitle: Observing or recording a person in a private place without consent is criminal
laws.fullDescription: Section 162 of the Criminal Code prohibits surreptitiously observing or recording a person in circumstances that give rise to a reasonable expectation of privacy for a sexual purpose. This includes hidden cameras in bathrooms, changing rooms, or bedrooms, as well as upskirt photography. Distribution of such recordings is separately criminalized under s.162.1. The proliferation of micro-cameras has led to hotel and Airbnb surveys by privacy-conscious travelers. Police have specialized units investigating these offences.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; sex offender registry in some circumstances
laws.exceptions: Authorized police surveillance under judicial authorization
